To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co-transplanting Schwann cells and mesenchymal stromal cells in a multichannle polymer scaffold promotes axon regeneration and functional recovery in rats with spinal cord injury.

a multichannel scaffold seeded with activated schwann cells and bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), when grafted into the transection gap after complete transection of the thoracic spinal cords in adult rats, promotes axonal regeneration and significantly improves functional recovery.
the co-transplantation with ASCs and bone marrow-derived MSCs in a polymer scaffold promotes axonal regeneration and improves functional recovery after spinal injury in adult rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for treating spinal cord injury (SCi) using a multichannel scaffold with Schwann cells and mesenchymal cells (MSCs).
the development of a novel combinatorially designed biomaterial for SCI treatment.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for spinal cord injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multichannel polymer scaffolds seeded with MSCs and ASCs can promote axonal regeneration, functional recovery, and host neuronal survival after spinal cord injury in adult rats.
the multichannel polymer seeded with ASCs plus MSCs can improve the functional recovery of rats following SCI.
the combination therapy with MSCs and Schwann cells in a multichannal scaffold may represent a promising strategy for the treatment for SCI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combinatorial therapy with Schwann cell and MSCs is more efficient for axon regeneration than either cell type alone.
we have shown that the co-implantation of activated Schwann cells with MSCs can promote axonal regeneration, functional recovery and neuroprotection after spinal cord injury.
the combination of ASCs and BMSCs can improve the functional recovery and the axonal regeneration in SCI rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of ASCs and rat bone marrow MSCs can promote axonal regeneration, functional recovery and neuronal differentiation of MSCs.
a combination of Schwann cells and mesenchymal stromal cells can be used to promote axonal growth and improve functional recovery after spinal injury.
the co-transplantation approach can be used for the repair of SCI.
